correctness.rationale: At a fixed product point P⊆X×Y, set Q={u:P_u∈G}. Rectangle □ means some U∈F,V∈G with U×V⊆P, while □1□2 means Q∈F. For finite nonempty upward-closed reflexive F,G, if {x}∈F then {x}×P_x works; if G binary-intersection closed, the finite intersection of P_u for u∈Q works. Conversely when singleton absent and G nonintersection closed, choose inclusion-minimal U∈F of size≥2 and B0,B1∈G with intersection not in G; sections B0/B1 over distinct members of U force □1□2 but any witness rectangle must use U and its vertical neighborhood would lie in the forbidden intersection. Transpose proves second equivalence. A nonintersection-closed reflexive family requires carrier≥3, so one reverse fail needs 2×3=6 and both need 3×3=9. Verified explicit 6- and 9-point truth sets; the 9-point valuation makes both iterated boxes true and rectangle box false. No infinite generalization.
